Purpose: One machine-readable answer to 'what can CircleAI actually do?', with two consumers:
1. An agent or developer navigating the repo — read this instead of 150 projects.
2. The SDK at runtime — loads this into the capability/skill registry so the
assistant can answer 'what can you do?' from fact instead of hallucination.
Status is the point. A feature that exists in name only says so here.

StatusDefinitions.shipping: Works end to end AND a test exercises the real behaviour (not a null object).
StatusDefinitions.partial: Works, with named caveats. Every limitation is listed in Limits.
StatusDefinitions.scaffold: Contracts, plumbing or a runtime exist; no working implementation behind them.
StatusDefinitions.planned: Declared surface or intent only. Nothing to call yet.
StatusDefinitions.rejected: Deliberately NOT being built. Reason is in Limits. Prevents rediscovery.

Conventions.EntryPoint: path/to/File.cs#Symbol — the single best place to START reading.
Conventions.Seam: The interface to implement or replace in order to extend/swap this.
Conventions.Requires: Obligations on the HOST. If unmet, the feature does not work.
Conventions.Limits: What it deliberately does NOT do. Absence of limits is itself a claim.
Conventions.VerifiedBy: Tests asserted to cover it. These are CLAIMS — CapabilityManifestTests validates them.
Conventions.Measured: Observed on REAL hardware, with numbers and a date. Never inferred from source.

Maintenance: This file is load-bearing, not documentation. A test asserts that every entry with
status 'shipping' resolves to a real symbol and names at least one real test.
If you cannot honestly write 'shipping', write what is true instead.
2026-07-20 — FIRST ON-DEVICE PASS. Huawei MAR-LX1M (P30 Lite, Kirin 710, ~1.1 GB
free RAM). Everything with a Measured block was observed on that handset. The pass
falsified FOUR claims previously written here from source-reading alone:
1. 'Native MNN libraries DO ship' — they do NOT reach an APK across a
ProjectReference. Inference died at DllNotFoundException after a good download.
2. 'the inference BRIDGE collapses a request to a single user message' — false.
Multi-turn history flows end to end.
3. 'No wake-word model exists, so Hey B cannot trigger' — false. There are TWO
detectors; the energy one needs no KWS model.
4. Voice was called untestable. Its VAD is pure DSP and testable with no weights.
Treat any entry WITHOUT a Measured block as source-reading, not evidence.

Capabilities.Name: Device-aware model selection
Capabilities.Summary: Picks the best model the current device can actually hold, from capability + RAM + storage.

Measured.Result: Selected Qwen3-0.6B-MNN, not the 14B. The MinRamGb gate is live.

Limits: Vision and Video are unsatisfiable — no such model is catalogued, so those requests throw by design.
Gates on RAM/storage only; ignores CPU, NPU and thermal headroom.
Gates on FIT, not on FUNCTION. There is no minimum-quality floor, so a device that can only hold an unusable model is handed it silently rather than told to use cloud fallback.

Capabilities.Name: Model catalogue
Capabilities.Summary: Nine SHA-pinned MNN model bundles (Qwen3 and Qwen2.5-Instruct ladders) with fallback chains.
Limits: Text LLMs only. No speech (ASR/TTS), no vision, no VAD, no wake-word entries — which is the single reason the voice stack cannot be acquired the same catalogue-driven way.
A second, older registry (src/CircleAI.Core/registry.json) still exists and can drift.

Capabilities.Name: Automatic model download
Capabilities.Summary: Fetches a model's multi-file bundle on first use, verifying every file by SHA-256.

Measured.Device: Huawei MAR-LX1M, over the phone's own WiFi
Measured.Result: 429 MB in 738 s (~580 KB/s). All 8 files. llm.mnn.weight = 450,810,338 bytes, atomically renamed from .tmp. installed.json stamped. No sideloading.

Limits: No AUTOMATED regression test — the proof above was a one-off manual device run, so this can silently break.

AIOptions.WifiOnlyModelDownload (default true) appears INERT: BundleModelLoader builds ModelDownloadService with no connectivity gate, so nothing observed stops a download on mobile data. Costs users money rather than failing loudly.

AIOptions carries two properties for one concept — ModelStorageDirectory (read by CheckForUpgradesAsync) and ModelStorageDir. The DI registration now prefers the former, but the duplication remains and both are public API.
LocalModelLoader (the older IModelLoader) still cannot fetch bundle entries and returns a path MNN cannot load.

Capabilities.Name: On-device inference (MNN)
Capabilities.Summary: Runs Qwen-family models locally through the MNN engine, streaming tokens as they decode.

Measured.Result: Qwen3-0.6B-MNN loaded in 19 s from cache. 576,347 KB resident native heap. Coherent multi-turn output incl. correct algebra. ~34 s per turn.

Requires: Model weights — none ship; smallest catalogued bundle is 433 MB.

CRITICAL for .NET Android hosts using a ProjectReference: the native libs live under src/CircleAI.Inference/runtimes/<rid>/native/, which is the NuGet PACKAGE convention. They do NOT flow across a ProjectReference, so the APK ships with zero MNN libraries and the first inference throws 'System.DllNotFoundException: mnnbridge'. The host must add explicit <AndroidNativeLibrary Include="...runtimes/android-arm64/native/*.so"><Abi>arm64-v8a</Abi></AndroidNativeLibrary> items. See samples/CircleAI.Samples.Android for the pattern.
On Android: AIOptions.NativeLibDir set to ApplicationInfo.NativeLibraryDir.
Limits: The SDK should ship a .targets file so Android consumers get the native libs automatically. Until then every consumer rediscovers this at runtime, not at build time.
~34 s per turn on a Kirin 710 is slow enough to be felt in UX.

Capabilities.Name: Tool calling
Capabilities.Summary: Describes registered tools to the model, parses its tool call, executes it, and feeds the result back.

Measured.Result: Both probes fired for real: get_battery_level() returned 100% (matched device truth) and lookup_price(sku=SKU-1001) returned 249.99 (matched the tool table). Arguments passed correctly. Invocation log proves execution, not just a plausible answer.

Limits: Until 2026-07-20 the DESCRIBE half did not exist: AvailableTools was referenced nowhere in CircleAI.Hosting, so a real model was never told a tool name and could only emit a valid call by guessing. Circle33ToolCallingTests stayed green throughout because its fake generator emits a canned <tool_call> regardless of the prompt.
The tools block is injected even when the caller owns the system turn — deliberate, since a registered bridge the model is never told about is a silent no-op.
No automated end-to-end test against a REAL model; the device run above is manual.
Verified with two trivial tools. Multi-tool disambiguation and multi-step tool chains are untested.

Capabilities.Name: Conversation memory and session snapshot
Capabilities.Summary: Threads full history through each turn and can snapshot the session to survive a restart.

Measured.Result: 'my name is Thabo' then 'what is my name?' -> 'Your name is Thabo.' Multi-turn recall works on device.

Limits: Snapshot round-trip covered only against a fake generator; a real restore of a real KV cache is untested.

PrepareMessagesAsync SKIPS persona / device-context / RAG enrichment entirely when the caller supplies its own system message. Tool descriptions are exempted, but the rest is silently dropped — hosts that own their system prompt lose enrichment without being told.
Notes: Corrected 2026-07-20: an earlier draft claimed the inference bridge collapsed a request to a single user message. That was WRONG. Traced end to end: NeuronNode.StreamAsync maps EVERY turn, AIService passes the whole list to PrepareMessagesAsync, and QwenTextGenerator renders all of it. `userQuery` is extracted only for routing and RAG lookup.

Capabilities.Name: Concierge routing
Capabilities.Summary: Decides per turn whether the warm generalist answers or a specialist should.

Measured.Result: 'hi' -> Generalist. 'solve x^2 = 49 step by step' -> Specialist (Reasoning) [reasoning cue 'solve']. The DECISION varies correctly per turn.

Limits: The decision is verified; ACTING on it is not. In the device run the specialist was never hot-loaded — only one model existed on disk — so the generalist answered both.
Vision routing requires RouteContext.HasImage and is unreachable from any text-only host.
Keyword and length heuristics only — no learned intent classification.

Capabilities.Name: Two-slot residency
Capabilities.Summary: Keeps one generalist permanently warm and admits a second specialist only if RAM allows.

Measured.Result: With Router set, a Specialist decision degraded gracefully to the generalist and answered — no throw. Graceful degradation on constrained hardware is PROVEN.

Limits: A real specialist has never been hot-loaded beside a real generalist. Only one model was on disk, so admission could not have succeeded and the fallback path is what actually ran.
Proving genuine two-slot residency needs a second catalogued model downloaded to the same device.

Capabilities.Name: Brownout and fallback chain
Capabilities.Summary: Under memory pressure, evicts the specialist and hot-swaps down to a smaller model.

Measured.Result: ManualMemoryPressureSource raised Critical; the next turn still answered normally. Pressure does not break serving.

Limits: Eviction ORDER is unproven: with no specialist resident there was nothing to evict, so 'specialist first, generalist never drops' was not actually exercised.
A real pressure-triggered model hot-swap has never been observed.

Capabilities.Name: Capability self-knowledge
Capabilities.Summary: Lets the assistant answer 'what can you do?' from THIS manifest rather than invention, and refuse to claim what it cannot yet do.

Measured.Result: Asked 'what can you do?' it answered accurately from the TOOLS block: 'retrieving battery level or looking up product prices'. This predates the feature-half wiring described in Limits.

Limits: The feature-half is now wired: CapabilityManifestSkillStore populates ISkillStore from THIS manifest, and CircleAISession.Skills composes it into the retrieval path ahead of the consumer pack and any user-uploaded skills. The 2026-07-20 Measured note above predates that wiring.

Every entry carries its Status, and non-shipping entries say 'not yet' in words the model cannot miss — so it will not claim voice, vision or the cross-app link as done. That honesty is the point, and it pairs with the persona's not-self-aware clause in CircleAISession.
Retrieval surfaces the top few MATCHED entries per turn, not a full enumeration — a broad 'what can you do?' sees a relevant sample, not the whole catalogue.
Covered by desktop tests (the store and its composition); NOT re-Measured on the P30 since the wiring landed.

Capabilities.Name: Everyday-life skill pack
Capabilities.Summary: Grounds answers to real South-African life tasks - a CV, a grant, tenant rights, a clinic visit, load-shedding, starting a small business, mental-health help, raising children - from a curated skill pack behind every grounded Services tile.
Limits: 34 skills covering every GROUNDED Services tile - money, work, small business, trades and land, health, family and home, and getting by. A test (Every_grounded_services_tile_has_a_skill_behind_it) fails if any grounded tile has no skill; the generative and creative tiles (write, translate, draw, look up, chat) are answered by the model and its tools, not a skill. South-Africa-first, and thin outside it.
Proven on the DESKTOP that every grounded tile opener reaches the retrieval engine and returns its skill; NOT yet Measured on the P30.

Runs from a prebuilt SQLite database (consumer.db, FTS5 + identifying match) unpacked once at first use - no Markdown is parsed on the turn path. The database IS the source of truth; the SKILL.md are not kept in the repo (one owner, no drift). Edit it via tools/skills-db --export then --consumer.

Guidance, not professional advice - the legal, medical, mental-health and money skills carry guardrails that point to the CCMA, clinics, Legal Aid, SADAG (0800 567 567), SASSA, NSFAS and the real emergency numbers rather than deciding for the user.

Capabilities.Name: User-uploaded skills
Capabilities.Summary: Lets a person add their own SKILL.md — from any source — into a writable store, so the assistant becomes customised to them.
Limits: The ingest and the writable SQLite store are tested and persist across restarts; there is NO user-facing upload screen yet, so from the app there is no way in — the repo's signature defect. It is wired via CircleAISession.UserSkills but not surfaced in UI.
Accepts one SKILL.md at a time (frontmatter + instructions). No pack/zip import, and no provenance check beyond a stamped source: label.
Junk — empty, unparseable, or no instructions — is refused and returns null; there are no partial writes.
Not Measured on the P30.

Capabilities.Name: On-device speech (ASR, TTS, wake word, VAD)
Capabilities.Summary: Local speech-to-text, text-to-speech, VAD and wake-word spotting with no cloud round trip.
Requires: Host-supplied weights for ASR and TTS. None ship and none are catalogued.
Limits: Only the VAD is covered. EnergyVadDetector now has 5 passing tests (silence, loud-then-silence, below-threshold hum, threshold flip on identical audio, stream ending mid-speech) — written 2026-07-20 because this file had wrongly called voice untestable.
No speech model is in the catalogue, so weights cannot be acquired the catalogue-driven way the LLM ladder uses. That — not missing code — is the actual blocker.
WhisperTranscriber and OnnxTtsEngine have never been run.
CircleAI.Speech and CircleAI.Voice define two overlapping, incompatible contract families.
Notes: Two claims previously in this file were WRONG and are corrected here:

(a) 'No wake-word model exists, so Hey B cannot trigger.' There are TWO detectors. KwsWakeWordDetector needs a KWS model; EnergyWakeWordDetector does NOT — it combines energy VAD with transcribe-and-string-match and its default wake word is literally 'hey b'. It does need a transcriber, and running one continuously is a battery problem, which is the real argument for a dedicated KWS model.
(b) 'Voice cannot be tested without weights.' EnergyVadDetector is pure managed DSP over PCM — no model, no microphone, no device.

Capabilities.Name: Cloud speech providers
Capabilities.Summary: Speech-to-text and text-to-speech via twelve hosted backends behind one contract.
Requires: Per-provider API keys — none supplied, so this is unverified against any live provider.
Limits: Batch only — no streaming partial transcripts.
Sends audio off-device, against the on-device-data stance. Opt-in fallback only.

Capabilities.Name: Platform speech wrapper (Android SpeechRecognizer / TextToSpeech)
Capabilities.Summary: Would use the phone's own recogniser and TTS — free, preinstalled, no model download.
Limits: REJECTED 2026-07-20 on the de-Googled rule. android.speech.SpeechRecognizer is Google-backed in practice, so it is a GMS dependency wearing an Android-framework costume. microG is not an acceptable substitute — it still proxies.
It also cannot run on the primary test handset: the Huawei P30 Lite has no GMS.

Nuance: android.speech.tts.TextToSpeech IS a pluggable framework, not inherently Google — eSpeak NG and RHVoice are installable engines. Platform TTS is therefore acceptable as a FALLBACK, but never a default, since it depends on the user having installed an engine.
Replaced by speech.catalogue (open stack).

Capabilities.Name: De-Googled speech model ladder
Capabilities.Summary: Open ASR + TTS models catalogued on Hugging Face, selected per device by modality — acquisition works; on-device synthesis does not yet.

Measured.Device: Windows x64 host — real ladder end to end, plus in the IT! sample
Measured.Result: TTS SYNTHESIS + FULL SAMPLE LOOP WORK. (1) Engine: IPA 'həlˈoʊ wˈɚld' → en_US-lessac-medium → 0.89 s @ 22050 Hz, RMS 0.1148 — real speech WAV. (2) IT! sample `--speak`: SpeechModelSelector picked Piper (Good) → ModelDownloadService fetched it from HuggingFace → espeak-ng phonemised → OnnxTtsEngine synthesised all 5 demo replies to WAVs whose durations track reply length (1.6 s 'IT out.' … 19.1 s reasoning reply), RMS 0.07–0.12. Arbitrary LLM-shaped text spoken, not fixed phonemes.

Requires: The ModelScope-only downloader was extended to Hugging Face (ModelSource.HuggingFace) so these are reachable.
Arbitrary English text → IPA needs espeak-ng (EspeakPhonemizer). Absent it, the engine still synthesises from supplied phonemes (PassthroughPhonemizer).
Limits: SYNTHESIS is now proven (Piper): OnnxTtsEngine was rewritten to feed phoneme ids in Piper's real BOS/pad/EOS layout from phoneme_id_map, at the config's sample rate — replacing the codepoint+1 stub that produced silence. Proven with real audio on a Windows host.

TEXT front end is the remaining seam: EspeakPhonemizer shells to espeak-ng, which is not present on every host and must be bundled + P/Invoked on Android/iOS. Where it is absent, arbitrary-text TTS does not run, but phoneme-in TTS does.

ASR NOW RUNS (closed 2026-07-21). The hand-rolled WhisperInterop still P/Invokes a whisper.dll that ships nowhere and would throw DllNotFoundException — so the runnable path is WhisperNetTranscriber, backed by Whisper.net, which bundles the whisper.cpp native library per-RID via NuGet (Whisper.net.Runtime). Proven: JFK sample transcribed VERBATIM (tools/stt-hear), and the IT! sample `--hear` transcribed IT!'s own spoken reply end to end. ACCURACY CAVEAT: ggml-tiny on SYNTHETIC (Piper) speech is rough — it heard 'It's easy to do…' for 'IT here. No, I won't ask…'; on natural human speech (JFK) it was verbatim. Tiny is the floor; a larger Whisper rung raises accuracy. Android/iOS need the matching Whisper.net.Runtime.<rid> package, same as the MNN native-lib story.
Not yet run on a physical device — the audio proof is a Windows host, not the Huawei.
Only the floor rung exists. Kokoro/LuxTTS (TTS) and Zipformer (streaming ASR) are not catalogued.
VAD and wake-word MODELS (ten-vad, openWakeWord) are still absent — EnergyVadDetector/EnergyWakeWordDetector already work without weights, so this is an upgrade not a floor gap.
FIT is not FUNCTION: MinRamGb/QualityRank are conservative estimates, not SelfBench measurements.
None of this covers South African languages (isiZulu, isiXhosa, Sesotho). English-first is shippable but a real competitive gap.

Capabilities.Name: Vision chat
Limits: No vision model is catalogued, so the selector can never choose one and Vision requests throw. That throw IS tested, so the current behaviour is honest — the feature simply does not exist.
KimiVlGenerator has never been executed.

Capabilities.Name: Standalone service link (other apps use this phone's brain)
Capabilities.Summary: CircleAI as a standalone service app other apps link to — install it once, authorise the model download, and let another app share this one brain instead of shipping its own, approving the link with a fingerprint, pattern or PIN.
Limits: The link LOGIC — scope, per-app grants, the gate's Allow/AutoApprove/NeedAuth/Deny decision, and the LinkTurn Parcel codec — is complete and unit-tested (LinkingTests, both frameworks). The cross-process Binder hop, the biometric consent screen, and two apps actually sharing one brain have NEVER run on a device.

Android transport (CircleNeuronLinkService, LinkConsentActivity, AndroidAuthChallenge) and the host client (CircleAI.Client) compile but are exercised by no automated cross-process test — there is no such harness off-device.
Default scope is chat only; memory and other domains' skills need a separate, higher grant.
First-party apps (same signing key) auto-grant; third-party apps require device auth on every link.

Capabilities.Name: Self-healing analysis
Capabilities.Summary: Given a failure (message + stack + context), categorises it and recommends quick-fix / patch / defer, drafting a patch when it can - a recommendation the consumer acts on, never an action Circle AI takes itself.
Requires: The Circle AI brain (IAIService) - the analyst is a thin layer over it.
Limits: Recommends and drafts only - it never acts. Executing a retry, opening a PR or deploying is the consumer's job (Circle AI is the brain, not the hand).

Unit-tested with a fake brain on the desktop; NOT yet Measured on the P30, and a 0.6B's JSON reliability under real load is unproven - an unparseable reply safely degrades to 'needs a human' rather than an invented fix.
In-process only for now (IFailureAnalyst); not yet exposed over the SDK registration, HTTP, or the on-device link for out-of-process consumers - those are later slices.
